problems.unknown: This component reported a problem. The details below come from it directly.

database.name: Database
database.description: PostgreSQL holds every model, collection, user and setting. Without it nothing in Thingport works.

problems.unreachable: Thingport can't reach the database. Check that the database container is running and that DATABASE_URL points at it, then restart the backend.
problems.timeout: The database didn't answer in time. It may be overloaded, or the host it runs on may be out of resources.

storage.name: File storage
storage.description: Where model files, their pictures and 3D previews are kept. Uploads, imports and downloads all need it writable, with room to spare.

problems.not_writable: Thingport can't write to its storage folder. Check that the volume is mounted, isn't read-only, and that PUID/PGID match the folder's owner.
problems.low_space: Storage is running low. New uploads and imports will fail once it's full: free up space or give the volume more.
problems.timeout: Checking the storage folder took too long. A network share may be slow or unavailable.

memory.name: Memory
memory.description: Building 3D previews of large models and simplifying them take the most memory. With too little, previews fail or the server restarts.

problems.low_memory: Memory is running low. Give the container more memory, or turn on Simplify previews under Rendering so heavy models need less.

internet.name: Internet
internet.description: Reaching the outside world from the server. Without it, providers can't be reached: importing models, syncing collections and checking for updates won't work.

problems.offline: The server can't reach the internet. Check its network, DNS and any proxy or firewall in front of it; Docker containers also need outbound access. Uploading and browsing your library still work.
problems.timeout: Nothing answered in time. The connection may be very slow, or something on the network is dropping requests.

flaresolverr.name: FlareSolverr
flaresolverr.description: Gets past Cloudflare's checks for providers that use them, mostly Thingiverse and Printables. Without it, imports and syncs from those sites will be blocked.

problems.not_configured: Not set up. Imports work until a provider shows a Cloudflare challenge; add a FlareSolverr URL so they keep working when it does.
problems.unreachable: FlareSolverr isn't answering. Check that its container is running and that the URL in Connections > FlareSolverr is right, including the port (usually 8191).
problems.timeout: FlareSolverr didn't answer in time. It may still be starting, or be busy.
problems.insecure: Working, but over plain HTTP to another machine, so provider cookies and API tokens cross the network unencrypted. Put FlareSolverr behind HTTPS, or run it in the same Compose stack as http://flaresolverr:8191.
problems.insecure_refused: FLARESOLVERR_REQUIRE_HTTPS is on, so this plain HTTP URL is refused and nothing is sent to it. Switch the URL to HTTPS, or remove the variable.
problems.https_ready: Connection is secure. Set FLARESOLVERR_REQUIRE_HTTPS=true to refuse insecure solver URLs from now on.

thingiverse.name: Thingiverse
thingiverse.description: The instance's Thingiverse App Token, used to import models, sync collections and liked models, and link authors from Thingiverse.

problems.disabled: Turned off under Providers, so nothing is checked. Turn Thingiverse back on there to use it.
problems.not_configured: No App Token set. Thingiverse imports and syncs won't work until one is added in Settings (create one at thingiverse.com/apps/create).
problems.token_rejected: Thingiverse rejected the App Token. Generate a new one at thingiverse.com/apps/create and save it in Settings.
problems.blocked: Thingiverse answered with a Cloudflare challenge, which says nothing about the token. Set up FlareSolverr, or wait: it usually clears after a while.
problems.unreachable: Thingport couldn't reach Thingiverse. Check the server's internet access, or try again later.
problems.timeout: Thingiverse didn't answer in time. Try again later.

myminifactory.name: MyMiniFactory
myminifactory.description: The instance's MyMiniFactory API key, used to read models, sync collections and link authors from MyMiniFactory. Free models download without it.

problems.disabled: Turned off under Providers, so nothing is checked. Turn MyMiniFactory back on there to use it.

fileReuse.heading: Identical files
fileReuse.subtitle: Save space when several users import the same model.
fileReuse.help: Thingport compares each new model file, supporting file, gallery image and description image with the ones already stored, whichever kind they are. Copy-on-write clones a match on btrfs, XFS or ZFS 2.2 and later, and stores the file as usual elsewhere. Thumbnails and renders aren't shared. Each clone is a file of its own, so editing one on disk never changes another user's. Files stored before it was turned on are checked too, see Existing files.

backfill.label: Existing files
backfill.help: Turning on cloning goes over the files already stored: each one's hash is recorded, then files with the same content are replaced by clones of the oldest one, keeping their own name, place and owner. Only files in Thingport's storage folder are touched, and a file that changes meanwhile is left as it is. Run it again after turning cloning on for a while off, or for files that couldn't be checked. Snapshots of the storage can keep the old copies, so the space freed is an upper bound.

extrude.title: Extrude
extrude.help: Pulls the sketch into a solid. Taper leans the sides in towards the far end (a draft); the ends' edges can be rounded or bevelled. Join, cut or intersect works it into another body.

revolve.title: Revolve
revolve.help: Turns the sketch about one of its axes. Its shapes must all be on one side of the axis.

press_pull.title: Press/pull
press_pull.help: Moves a flat face straight out (adds) or in (cuts), keeping its outline.

fillet.title: Fillet
fillet.help: Rounds straight edges between flat faces. Outside edges are rounded off, inside edges filled. Click edges to add or remove them.

chamfer.title: Chamfer
chamfer.help: Bevels straight edges between flat faces, cutting back the same distance on both. Click edges to add or remove them.

hole.title: Hole
hole.help: Drills a round hole where you click, into the surface. Counterbore and countersink make room for a screw head.

shell.title: Shell
shell.help: Hollows the body, with walls of this thickness. Click flat faces to leave them open, like a tray's top.

split.title: Split
split.help: Splits the body in two: by a plane, a flat face's plane, or another body. Both parts stay editable.
split.pickTool: Click the body to split by

scale.title: Scale
scale.help: Scales the body about its own origin.

sketch_face.title: Sketch on a face
sketch_face.help: Starts a sketch on the flat face you click.
sketch_face.pick: Click a flat face to sketch on

separate.title: Separate parts
separate.help: Makes each loose part of the body, each piece that doesn't touch the rest, a body of its own. A hollow inside a part stays with it; parts that overlap without being joined stay apart, each in its own colour here. Deleting all the parts gives the body back.
separate.open_one: {{count}} has gaps: it can be moved and exported, not combined
separate.open_other: {{count}} have gaps: they can be moved and exported, not combined

text.title: Text
text.help: Writes words as a solid: raised letters on a plane, or embossed or engraved on a body's flat face. Letter height is a capital's height; 6 mm or more prints well. The words, font and size stay editable on its sketch.
text.pick: Click a flat face to write on

pattern.title: Pattern
pattern.help: Repeats a body in a row, a grid or round an axis, and makes the copies one body with it. Change the body and every copy follows. To cut many holes, pattern one hole's cylinder and subtract the pattern.

mirror.title: Mirror
mirror.help: Mirrors a body across a plane, for something symmetric built one half at a time. Keeping the original makes the half and its mirror image one body.

align.title: Align
align.help: Lines a body up with another body, or with the bed: its starts, middles or ends together, or beside it (before or after) with a gap. On Z, after puts it on top. It only moves the body.
align.pickReference: Click a body to line it up with, or leave it lined up with the bed

lay_flat.title: Lay flat
lay_flat.help: Turns a body so the face you click lies on the bed, as you would turn a part for printing, and sets it down on the bed.
lay_flat.pick: Click the face to lay it on

sweep.title: Sweep
sweep.help: Moves the sketch's outline along a path of points and makes the solid it passes through: a pipe, a handle, a rail. The sketch's origin rides on the path, so draw the outline around it; it starts square to the path at the first point. Smooth runs a curve through the points, Closed makes a ring.

imported.parts_one: The model came in as one body of {{count}} part
imported.parts_other: The model came in as one body of {{count}} separate parts

trace.title: Trace picture
trace.help: Turns a picture's shapes into an outline to make solid: a logo, a silhouette, lettering, a drawing. Dark shapes on a light background are traced (Invert for light on dark; see-through counts as light), and holes stay holes. A clean picture with strong contrast traces best.

path.title: Add path
path.help: SVG path data in the sketch's millimetres, x to the right and y up: M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, T, A and Z, each subpath one closed outline. Paste one from a drawing program or write it by hand.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.help: Named numbers the design's sizes can follow. In any size field, type = and a formula, such as =wall * 2 + 10. Change a parameter here and every formula that uses it is worked out again.
parameters.name: Name
parameters.inUse: In use: change the fields that follow it first
parameters.badName: Letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit

check.title: Check for printing
check.help: Checks each visible body where it's placed: on the bed and within it, in one piece, not overlapping another, with no overhang that needs support and no wall too thin to print. It's the same check the assistant runs on its own work.

measure.title: Measure
measure.help: Pick points, edges, faces or bodies. One pick shows its own size: a point's position, an edge's length, a face's area, a body's size and volume. Two show the shortest distance between them, how far apart that is along X, Y and Z, and the angle between them. Readings are in the status bar's units, and measuring doesn't change the design.
